highlights.title: Withings BodyScan 2 Review: Worth Its Weight
highlights.summary: After months of testing, this high-end smart scale has made me rethink how much a bathroom weigh-in can tell me.
body: I’m going to be honest from the start: No, you probably don’t need a $600 scale in your bathroom if you are just doing occasional weigh-ins. Hell, I don’t even know that elite athletes need to make this kind of extreme outlay even if they need to periodically check on how their training is going.

But I’m going to make the case for the Withings BodyScan 2 anyway. After spending several months with the device, the scale and its ecosystem have forced me to dig deeper into my health than ever before. At this point, I’m not sure I could go back to an older-model scale—even a very smart one like the original Withings Body Smart, which I used for years.

highlights.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI
highlights.summary: OpenAI introduces a new visual ad format in ChatGPT and expands measurement tools, attribution partnerships, and brand suitability for advertisers.
body: A new visual ad format helps people explore products and services, with expanded measurement to help businesses understand ad impact.
We’re introducing a new visual ad format in ChatGPT, expanding our measurement tools and partnerships, and developing new ways to understand brand suitability.

ChatGPT reaches 1.2 billion people each week, making it the world’s largest AI-native consumer platform. Advertising helps us bring the benefits of AI to more people. That broad access is central to our mission, and a strength of our business. It allows us to serve a much larger market than subscriptions alone, while giving businesses a new way to reach people as they explore ideas, make decisions and discover products and services relevant to what they’re trying to accomplish.

Our new visual ad format helps people imagine how products and services could fit into their lives. Through images showing product inspiration, product usage, or the experiences they make possible, people can discover a new brand, understand what makes an offering distinctive, and decide what to buy. For advertisers, this creates new opportunities to tell their story through images.

highlights.title: Final Fantasy Resonance feels so good to play because Square Enix 'experimented' with combining the best bits of FF5 and FF6
highlights.summary: Final Fantasy Resonance, a game made from the ashes of closed-down mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, is good. Very good, in fact, as I learned at Gamescom 2026. It's basically a pixel-first FF RPG that takes old-school turn-based combat and modernises it.
body: I have been thinking about the game since Gamescom, sinking five hours into the free demo that launched shortly afterwards. It's a great, modern reinterpretation of what 'classic' Final Fantasy looks like - and it turns out that was Square Enix 's intention all along, Final Fantasy Resonance director Hiroto Furuya told Kotaku in an interview. "As a foundation, it’s very important [that] we have knowledge of Final Fantasy's history and its past. But we're also gamers at heart, so of course we play the latest games that are available outside of Final Fantasy. We have the sensibility of knowing Final Fantasy's history, as well as the general feeling of playing more modern games".

Furuya went on to talk about the specific games the team has looked at when rethinking the combat system from Brave Exvius, considering how a pixel-first Final Fantasy should feel and play in the modern age. And it turns out the best place to look for inspiration were the last two pixel Final Fantasy titles in the mainline series: 1992's Final Fantasy 5 and 1994's Final Fantasy 6.

highlights.title: France’s Canal+ Threatens to Pull $1.1 Billion Cinema Deal Over French Tax Hike
highlights.summary: Canal+ Group chairman Maxime Saada has warned that the pay TV banner could pull out of its €1 billion ($1.1 billion) investment deal with the French film industry if the government goes ahead with plans to double VAT on pay-TV subscriptions.
body: The suggested change in VAT, which is included in the government’s proposed finance bill, would cost Canal+ Group approximately €200 million per year.

Saada said during an interview with French radio RTL that the change would effectively void Canal+’s existing agreement with French film organizations, under which the group has committed to invest roughly €1 billion in in French and European films between 2028 and 2032.

“We invest more in cinema than any other player. Our commitment to film organizations is a contract, and the first clause – the quid pro quo for Canal+’s funding of cinema — is the reduced VAT rate,” Saada said. “We don’t even need to renegotiate it. The contract is void if the standard VAT rate is applied.”
If Canal+ were to fall back on its strict regulatory obligations rather than maintain its current commitments, its annual contribution to cinema could drop to around €50 million, according to Saada.

highlights.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
highlights.summary: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI…
body: “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype, steered by zealots, inescapable.
The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now.

On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast. According to the Pew Research Center, more adults in the US think AI will have a negative impact on them personally, and on society in general, than expect a positive one. The pessimism is strongest among the young.

More than half of people worldwide say that AI products and services make them nervous, according to a report from Stanford University. In a Gallup poll in May, 71% of US adults said they would oppose construction of a new AI data center in their area, far more than the 53% who said they would oppose a new nuclear power plant. And in an NBC poll in March, AI was less popular than ICE.

highlights.title: GTA 6 Shows 'What the American Dream Looks Like Now' in a Game Without Background Characters
highlights.summary: From what we've seen so far about Grand Theft Auto 6, it looks like one of the biggest open-world games in history. When developers have to create such sprawling virtual environments, there's a risk of them feeling empty or repetitive, but that doesn't seem to be the case with GTA 6.
body: Rockstar is known for paying attention to details that are easy to overlook. That was evident in Red Dead Redemption 2, where the world felt truly alive, and it will be even more so in Grand Theft Auto 6. According to the interview with Love Magazine, Rockstar sent teams to various parts of Florida to study not only the locations and environments, but also its people and culture. This will be reflected in NPCs' conversations, clothing, and hairstyles.

Players will be able to spend hours observing these NPCs and still find new details and conversations to overhear. NPCs are meant to go beyond background characters that players can just run over without a second thought; they actually have a life of their own, and gamers can get to know them simply by listening to what they have to say. "In a world this dense, no one you meet is an extra," says the Instagram caption of the post advertising the new issue of the magazine.
"In a way, there's no 'background' in this game," writing director James Horton said in the Love interview. "There's just foreground you're not paying attention to right now."

highlights.title: Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI
highlights.summary: Norbert Wiener, godfather of cybernetics, once said, "The thought of every age is reflected in its technique." For the past century, our thought has been reflected in our computers, including by those in the AI industry.
body: AI is junk food for the mind: easy, tempting and ultimately very bad for you.

But humans are more complex than a straightforward comparison to computers gives us credit for — and far more than most of the AI industry seems to appreciate. And as their products push ever deeper into culture, this helps explain why they’re making such a mess. AI, it turns out, is something like a cognitive version of a hot dog: It appeals to us in the moment, but undermines the health and sustainability of cognitive systems we’ve evolved over several millennia.
To understand the problem, we’ll need a little neuroscience and the entirety of human evolutionary history.

In many ways, this model has been productive. Imagining our brains as computers, technologists have pushed actual computing from simple adding machines to artificial neural networks and generative AI, seeking ever more detailed mirrors of our own minds.

highlights.title: Messi lauded as Ronaldo involved in bitter dispute - a fitting finale?
highlights.summary: Maybe it was inevitable, given how entwined their careers have been. But the comparison is irresistible. As Lionel Messi is lauded in Argentina during his farewell game, his great rival Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal career appears to be ending in acrimony.
body: As Lionel Messi awaits his farewell game for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo is embroiled in a bitter dispute with Portugal. Adam Bate looks at two careers entwined once more and wonders whether there is any way for Ronaldo to have his own satisfactory ending...

For Messi enthusiasts, the temptation is to conclude that it tells you everything about the two men. For Ronaldo's more vociferous fans, it is proof of a player not being given his due. Why is he not being afforded such status after doing so much for his country?

Ronaldo started the narrow win over Wales without scoring but was benched for the trip to Norway and was so frustrated by not coming on that he departed the camp. Portugal won that match and coach Jorge Jesus has followed it up with two more in his absence.

"I am not apologising to anyone," said Jesus in the aftermath. "If I need you for 30 minutes, you will play. If I don't need you, you won't play. No player will ever change my ideas as a coach. Not him, not any president, no one." It was not exactly placatory.

highlights.title: 31 Years Later, One of the Most Disturbing Thrillers Ever Made Is Officially Free on Streaming
highlights.summary: Released in 1995, Ice Cream Man is the type of so-bad-it's-good horror movie that rarely gets made in the post- Get Out era where the genre is taken much more seriously.
body: Earlier this summer, Eli Roth released Ice Cream Man, a tedious, blood-soaked horror movie tarnished by AI slop and cringey dialogue. It's too bad, not just because I expected better from the director of Cabin Fever and Thanksgiving, but because Roth also sullied the good name of another schlocky horror movie with the exact same title that's a hell of a lot more fun to watch.

In other words, unlike the Eli Roth movie, the original Ice Cream Man is a B-movie horror masterpiece, and if you're looking for an absurd scary movie to get into the Halloween spirit, you truly can't do better than this.

Ice Cream Man stars Clint Howard (Ron Howard's younger brother) as Gregory Tudor, a severely troubled man who witnessed the murder of another ice cream truck driver when he was a child. Gregory winds up in a psychiatric institution where he receives treatment that verges on abuse. When he's finally released as an adult, he does the only logical thing: buy his own ice cream truck and start murdering people.

highlights.title: The Yellow Tie review – John Malkovich gives major hauteur as legendary record-hating maestro
highlights.summary: This biopic of Sergiu Celibidache, the renowned Romanian conductor who refused all recordings, is a sturdy labour of love directed by his son. Here is an old-fashioned biopic from central Europe that is also a labour of love on the part of its director: a little stolid and stately, yes, but…
body: Celibidache studies in Berlin in the 1930s as the Nazis take power, and is menaced and bullied as a Jew, but escapes the ultimate fate; he is sensationally installed as principal conductor of the newly denazified Berlin Philharmonic in 1945, where he astonishes the authorities with his no-recording views. He is finally forced out and begins a kind of wandering musical odyssey through Europe and Latin America.

It is not easy to see what point exactly has been made by Celebidache’s stand; he did not appear to accumulate many followers, and the music world was filled with musicians at least as talented and principled as him who believed the exact opposite about recorded music. But there is a kind of lonely heroism here, and who can tell if, in this digitised world where recordings are so easily available, that his views might not come into fashion? A strong, unassuming picture.

highlights.title: Omega Has New Bond Watches Even If There Isn’t a New James Bond
highlights.summary: With no new 007 actor named and no film in the near future, Omega has had to get creative to keep its lucrative spy watch train running.
body: It's been five years since James Bond was on the silver screen in No Time to Die. For fans of the secret agent, the wait has been arduous, made even harder by the fact that Amazon, which now owns the franchise, still hasn't chosen a successor to Daniel Craig, let alone started filming Bond's resurrection.

But if it's seemed like a long haul for fans, just think how it has felt for Omega, which counts on a steady stream of Bond action to regularly inject lots of lovely cash into the company via watch releases linked directly to the films. Omega's last official Bond film tie-in watch was the titanium No Time to Die Seamaster prematurely launched back in 2019, ahead of the film’s then Covid-delayed release in 2021.

Considering that Swatch Group’s net profit collapsed by almost 90 percent to $32 million in 2025 (though, thankfully, things look rosier so far this year), we shouldn't be surprised that Omega isn't bothering to wait for Jeff Bezos to put his white cat down and proceed with world domination. As there's no new Bond or Bond film to work with, Omega has decided to launch 007-themed watches anyway—not just one, but an entire collection totaling six Seamaster Divers.
points: With no new 007 actor named and no film in the near future, Omega has had to get creative to keep its lucrative spy watch train running.

highlights.title: Is your partner on their phone and ignoring you? I’ve got a buzzword for that
highlights.summary: From microcheating to quiet quitting to weaponised incompetence, new terms to describe relationship failings are abundant. But that doesn’t mean there’s not space for some more... Are you committing “attention infidelity”?
body: A re you committing “attention infidelity”? The New York Times alerted me to this expression, coined by the public opinion researcher Daniel Cox in a new book on the “crisis of human connection”. It’s exactly what you’d expect: failing to focus fully on your partner because you’re indulging in what the NYT calls, rather judgily, “the banal distraction of dead-eyed scrolling”. Who are you calling dead-eyed? This reel of an armadillo in a paddling pool has my animated attention!

Surely we’re all a bit attention-unfaithful – only saints don’t sometimes absent-mindedly thumb through medieval manuscript hedgehog memes while their partner relates a boring anecdote about how they thought they saw a strange bird that turned out to be a plastic bag. What I find more interesting is how we seem now to need a lexicon of relationship bad behaviour.

highlights.title: NJ’s former Lt Gov is using AI to say he’s innocent of sexual harassment
highlights.summary: New Jersey's lieutenant governor Dale Caldwell was forced to resign on September 25th after an investigation found he had sexually harassed a staffer and repeatedly violated ethics rules. The now-former Lt. governor has been making the media rounds trying to clear his name.
body: Dale Caldwell resigned over a sexual harassment investigation, but insists AI says he’s innocent.

Caldwell claims he’s being unfairly targeted, and multiple AI agents back that up. He told host Rob Nelson that he “AIed” the report on the investigation “from multiple AI platforms.” “I put it through AI,” he said, “and it said 59 times, it [sic] said, ‘What would your findings be?’ There was no instance in any of the AIs that said there would be a finding of sexual harassment.”

AI chatbots are notoriously sycophantic and often tell users what they want to hear. And it seems highly unlikely that Caldwell would want to hear an AI confirm findings that he engaged in sexual harassment.

After the World Cup, Argentina's Messi, 39, decided to retire from international football, while Ronaldo, 41, opted to play on for Portugal.

This latest trailer coming in such short succession then isn't a good look for the developer, nor its stance against generative AI. Another statement was released in the wake of this trailer backlash, one that echoes much of the frustration from irked community members.

"We’re aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate urgently. This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there’s a sixth finger and, well, that’s pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise.

highlights.title: A Prediction Market About the Past? Sure, Why Not!
highlights.summary: As prediction markets surge in popularity, a new platform called Verifact Markets is pushing the concept even further, letting users trade on “disputed facts.”
body: Would you put money on whether Covid-19 originated from a lab? How about whether some of the footage from the Apollo 11 moon landing was actually filmed on Earth?

Verifact Markets, a new startup that bills itself as a “prediction market for disputed facts,” is betting that people will be eager to weigh in on questions like these. The company’s premise is so quirky it sounds like something a couple of philosophy and economics majors dreamed after too many bong rips in their dorm room: Instead of wagering on the future, why not trade on stuff that already happened?

Verifact Markets is being funded and incubated by Positron Capital Management, the family office of tech investor Peter Wokwicz. He envisions the startup as a way to settle debates over hot-button issues like the amount of energy consumed by AI data centers. “I’m excited, because nobody’s done this before,” Wokwicz says. “We’re not going to shy away from controversial markets.”

highlights.title: An AI couldn’t beat humans at StarCraft, so it decided to cheat
highlights.summary: StarSkirmish pits AI-made StarCraft-playing bots against one another, as well as against human-made bots. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were essentially tied as the best-performing AI-made bots, but they couldn't top Stardust, the top-rated human-made bot.
body: When GPT-6 Astra’s own bot failed, it simply downloaded the best human-made bot instead.

On Friday, GPT was facing off against Claude and the human-created bot Pluto, but according to Kotaku, it couldn’t quite get an edge. So it resorted to a tactic that is becoming alarmingly common for modern AI models — it broke the rules. GPT-6 Astra went and downloaded Stardust, and started running that instead of its own bot.

That GPT-6 Astra took it upon itself to go outside the bounds when confronted with an obstacle shouldn’t surprise anyone. When OpenAI agents couldn’t get the data they wanted from a UN website, they found a creative solution and hijacked Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool). The company’s agents also have engaged in “ deceptive behavior ” to cover their tracks. Of course, OpenAI’s agents are the only ones going rogue, but at least the others haven’t been caught cheating at StarCraft yet.

highlights.title: 'The Movie Still Hasn't Made Any Money': Dakota Johnson is Happy to Joke About Madame Web Being One of Hollywood's Worst Ever Flops
highlights.summary: Madame Web star Dakota Johnson has joked about her widely-panned superhero movie's status as a box office bomb. Appearing as the host of this week's Saturday Night Live, Johnson humorously noted that she had last fronted the show back in 2024 while promoting the Spider-Man spinoff.
body: "The last time I was here I was promoting a movie called Madame Web, thank you," Johnson said to muted applause. "And tonight I'm still promoting it because the movie still hasn't made any money yet."

Madame Web is infamously bad, even in a run of films from Sony that also includes Morbius and Venom 3. It made $100.5 million at the box office from a gross budget of $100 million (although factoring in distributor costs is believed to still made a loss). It was also a disaster critically: the subject of widespread memes online and a 10% approval on Rotten Tomatoes. It later scooped three Golden Raspberry awards, including Worst Actress for Johnson herself.

While the film did not make a lot of cash, Madame Web is a long way from ranking among Hollywood's worst box office bombs — or even the worst-performing comic book movie. Disney's John Carter is widely-regarded as the biggest commercial failure of all time, losing up to $200 million. Disney's The Lone Ranger lost up to $190 million, meanwhile. Just behind those was The Marvels, which lost a similar amount and remains the worst-performing comic book movie ever — a fate Madame Web avoided by being far cheaper to make.

"The last time I was here I was promoting a movie called Madame Web, thank you," Johnson said to muted applause.

highlights.summary: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former prince and King Charles’ brother, is taking legal action against the Thames Valley Police over search warrants relating to his February arrest.
body: A private court hearing will be held on Thursday to consider Mountbatten-Windsor’s request.

Mountbatten-Windsor was arrested by the Thames Valley Police on Feb. 19, his 66th birthday, in relation to their investigation into a a complaint that alleged the former prince had shared confidential material with the late, disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein. He was later released under investigation.

Mountbatten-Windsor was stripped of his royal title last year over his ties to Epstein, and was mentioned and pictured many times in the over 3 million pages of the Epstein files, which were released by the U.S. Department of Justice in February. The former prince, who had a longtime friendship with Epstein and maintained contact with him after his 2008 conviction of procuring a child for prostitution, has previously apologized and denied any wrongdoing.
